gen-gf-underdog-gf-padyakke-expanded-one: Padyakke Expanded One is a serif with wide, pitcher-mouthed curves. Over a full page its round bowls and loosely strung glyphs read slowly and with weight, while Underdog stays the loud one above.
gen-dafont-nasalization-fs-quicksand: Friendly letters float apart in Nasalization, short-ascendered and wide-set. Quicksand follows with tall, rounded lowercase bowls and bar strokes of identical weight, so it holds up nicely at a modest size.
gen-dafont-neuropolitical-fs-pilcrow-rou: Pulled-apart neon tubing, that's Neuropolitical, and it earns its keep big and short. Pilcrow Rounded tucks its letters tight, with large counters in a tall lowercase and curves that refuse to close.
gen-dafont-nordic-fs-hind: Widely spaced, tight-mouthed Nordic feels ancient and powerful, monoweight throughout. Hind's c never turns inward, so tight heading letters meet open body letters, and that clash is the whole appeal.
gen-dafont-oldtimer-fs-spline-sans: Open parentheses for letters: Oldtimer is classic and commanding. Spline Sans gives wide gaps at curve ends and uniform strokes, so the pair's real strength is old-school swagger meeting a modern, approachable body.
gen-dafont-origami-fs-nunito: Nunito reads soft and approachable, with big round lowercase bowls and terminals that stop well short of the stem. Origami, tube-like through every bend, wants generous size to show it.
gen-gf-warnes-poppins: Poppins is modern and clean, with a sturdy, tall-bodied lowercase. Above it, Warnes spreads out in stretched, spacious tracking with tapering ink strokes, while Poppins gives the eye no thick-thin flicker.
gen-gf-grandstander-manrope: Letters held open, short ascenders, tall x-height: that's Grandstander. Grandstander is best at shouting in constant-width lines, while Manrope, the sans-serif, is best at bright open curves and a small cap-to-lowercase step.
gen-gf-bellota-outfit: Stylus-width strokes and a drifting s: Bellota earns its keep big and short. Outfit, the sans-serif, bends cable-like curves that stop well before they close, with no swelling or thinning.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-fs-spline-sans: Ruler-straight lines with a beat per character: that's Bruno Ace. Spline Sans brings wide curve gaps and uniform strokes, so the best trait here is a slow, lingering heading resting on a friendly, modern body.
